title: Noble Group halts share trading after bond default
主要内容: Noble Group, once Asia's largest commodity trader, halted share trading after defaulting on a $394 million bond that matured this week. The company, based in Hong Kong, is seeking a $3.4 billion debt restructuring plan, which is seen as critical for its survival. The restructuring deal has faced opposition from some bondholders and shareholders, including Goldilocks Investment Co, which holds an 8.1 percent stake in the firm. Goldilocks filed a lawsuit with a Singapore court against Noble and some of its former and current senior executives, alleging they inflated Noble's assets. Noble has stated it plans to vigorously resist any allegations. The company's market value has plummeted to $114 million from $6 billion in February 2015, due to record losses and a shrinking business. Noble has been negotiating a debt-for-equity swap for months after selling billions of dollars in assets and cutting hundreds of jobs over the past three years. The company confirmed that a group of senior creditors now holds 50 percent of its debt and expects more lenders to support the restructuring plan.
